heading: AND CHILDREN FROM ACTS OF VIOLENCE.
translated_text:
AND CHILDREN FROM ACTS OF VIOLENCE.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean:

1. Region is the Special Capital Region Province of Jakarta, hereinafter referred to as DKI Jakarta Province.
2. 3. 4. Regional Government is the Governor and Regional Apparatus of DKI Jakarta Province as elements of the administration of DKI Jakarta Province government.

The Regional House of Representatives of the Special Capital Region Province of Jakarta, hereinafter referred to as DPRD, is a regional representative institution of the people as an element of regional government administration.

The Governor is the Regional Head of DKI Jakarta Province who by virtue of his/her position also serves as the representative of the Government in the DKI Jakarta Province region.

5. Regional Apparatus Work Unit, hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD, is the Apparatus of DKI Jakarta Province.
6. 7. 8. 9. Regional Apparatus Work Unit, hereinafter abbreviated as UKPD, is the Regional Apparatus Work Unit of DKI Jakarta Province.

Discrimination is any distinction, harassment or exclusion, whether direct or indirect, based on human differentiation on the grounds of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs that results in the reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life, whether individual or collective, in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural and other aspects of life.

Violence is any act unlawfully with or without the use of means against physical and psychological that causes danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom.

Violence against women is any act based on gender difference that results in or may result in suffering or hardship to women physically, sexually or psychologically, economic or social exploitation, including threats of certain acts, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.

10. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in suffering or hardship physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, economic or social exploitation, including neglect and ill-treatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child.
11. Domestic violence is any act against a person, especially women, that results in suffering or hardship physically, sexually, psychologically and/or household neglect including threats to commit acts of coercion or deprivation of freedom unlawfully within the scope of the household.

or

12. Trafficking in Persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, transfer, harboring, or receipt of persons by means of the threat or use of force, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud and abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payments or benefits to obtain the consent of a person having control over another person, whether conducted within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the exploitation of persons.
13. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years including a child still in the womb.
14. Woman is a person (human being) who has a vagina, can menstruate, become pregnant, give birth to children, and breastfeed.
15. Victim of violence is an individual or group of people who suffer physically, mentally or emotionally, economic loss, or experience neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights, as a result of human rights (HAM) violations, or criminal acts as well as acts of violence committed either by state apparatus or by the state or regional government apparatus or by individuals, including the victim's heirs.
16. Protection is a series of fulfillment of the rights of women and children victims of violence and discrimination starting from prevention, handling and empowerment efforts.
17. Prevention is a direct effort undertaken by the Regional Government to prevent acts of violence against women and children.
18. Integrated Service Center for the Empowerment of Women and Children, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is an Integrated Service Unit established by the Regional Government to provide services to women and children victims of violence comprehensively including information services, legal assistance and accompaniment, counseling services, medical services and safe houses through referral.
19. Task Force for the Prevention and Handling of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons, hereinafter referred to as the Task Force, is a coordinating institution tasked with coordinating prevention and handling efforts of the crime of trafficking in persons in DKI Jakarta Province.
20. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or mother.
21. Family are persons who have blood relations in direct ascending or descending line and collateral line up to the third degree, or who have marital relations, or persons who are dependents of women and/or children.
22. Community are individuals, families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations.

CHAPTER IV

OBLIGATIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Article 6

Obligations and responsibilities in providing protection to women and children from acts of violence are the shared responsibility of:

a. Regional Government;
b. Community;
c. Family; and
d. Parents.

heading: Article 7
Article 8
translated_text:
Article 8

1. The obligations and responsibilities of the community as referred to in Article 6 letter b, shall be implemented in the form of community participation.
2. Forms of community participation as referred to in paragraph (1), include:a. preventing the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children;
b. providing information and/or reporting acts of violence against women and children to law enforcement or authorized parties; danc. participating in the handling of victims of acts of violence.

Forms of community participation as referred to in paragraph (2), shall be implemented responsibly in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

heading: Article 9
translated_text:
Article 9

The obligations of the family and/or parents as referred to in Article 6 letter c and letter d, who legally have full responsibility to prevent all forms of violence and protect women and children as family members.

Article 13

Article 14

heading: CHAPTER VII
translated_text:
CHAPTER VII

INSTITUTIONAL ARRANGEMENTS

Article 16

1. In the context of providing protection services to women and children from acts of violence, the Regional Government establishes P2TP2A as an integrated service center for the protection of women and children from acts of violence including victims of acts of violence.
2. P2TP2A as referred to in paragraph (1), functions as an integrated service center in providing protection to women and children from acts of violence.
3. Further provisions regarding the Organization and Working Procedures of P2TP2A as referred to in paragraph (1), shall be stipulated by a Governor Regulation.

heading: Article 17
translated_text:
Article 17

In addition to establishing P2TP2A as referred to in Article 16, in order to support the implementation of the provision of protection to women and children from acts of violence, the Governor establishes:
a. task force on trafficking in persons;
b. regional action committee for the elimination of the worst forms of child labor.

heading: Article 18
translated_text:
Article 18

1. The task force as referred to in Article 17 letter a, shall consist of representatives from the Regional Government, law enforcement, community organizations, non-governmental organizations, professional organizations, and researchers/academics.
2. The task force as referred to in paragraph (1), is a coordinative body tasked with coordinating the prevention and handling of trafficking in persons.
3. Further provisions regarding the establishment, duties, and functions of the task force as referred to in paragraph (1), shall be stipulated by a Governor Regulation.

heading: Article 19
translated_text:
Article 19

1. The committee as referred to in Article 17 letter b, shall consist of representatives from the Regional Government, law enforcement, community organizations, non-governmental organizations, professional organizations, and researchers/academics.
2. Further provisions regarding the duties and functions of the committee as referred to in paragraph (1), shall be stipulated by Governor Decree.

heading: CHAPTER VIII
translated_text:
CHAPTER VIII

COOPERATION AND PARTNERSHIP

Part One Cooperation

Article 20

1. In order to achieve the objectives of protecting women and children from acts of violence as referred to in Article 3, the Regional Government cooperates with:
a. the Government;
b. other provinces;
c. Regencies/Cities; and
d. non-governmental institutions.
2. Cooperation as referred to in paragraph (1) includes:
a. exchange of data and information;
b. rehabilitation of victims of acts of violence;
c. repatriation and social reintegration; and
d. provision of evidence and witnesses.
e. followed up in accordance with applicable law
3. Cooperation as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) shall be set forth in the form of a Joint Agreement.

heading: Part Two Partnership
translated_text:
Part Two Partnership

Article 21

1. The Regional Government establishes partnerships with the business community in the protection of women and children from acts of violence.
2. Partnership as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out through:
a. notification of employment opportunity information for women victims of acts of violence;
b. education and training for women victims of acts of violence;
c. educational assistance for women and children victims of acts of violence who have been withdrawn from their education; and
d. fostering and enhancing the economic independence of women victims of acts of violence.
3. Partnership as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2), shall be set forth in the form of an agreement.

heading: CHAPTER IX
translated_text:
CHAPTER IX

GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION

Article 22

1. The Regional Government is obliged to conduct guidance and supervision of the implementation of protection of women and children from acts of violence.
2. Guidance as referred to in paragraph (1), includes:
a. guidelines and fulfillment standards;
b. technical guidance and training;
c. provision of facilities;
d. monitoring; and
e. evaluation.
3. Guidance as referred to in paragraph (2), is in order to realize the objectives of protecting women and children from acts of violence in accordance with minimum service standards implemented by SKPD/UKPD and the community.

heading: Article 23
translated_text:
Article 23

1. The Regional Government is obliged to conduct supervision of the implementation of protection of women and children from acts of violence.
2. Supervision as referred to in paragraph (1), is carried out with professional, transparent, and accountable principles.

heading: Article 24
translated_text:
Article 24

The community may conduct supervision of the implementation of protection of women and children from acts of violence organized by the Regional Government with a mechanism for conveying aspirations to the Governor or to the DPRD.

heading: CHAPTER X
translated_text:
CHAPTER X

FINANCING

Article 25

Financing for the implementation of protection of women and children from acts of violence is sourced from:

a. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget (APBD); and
b. other lawful sources in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

heading: Article 26
translated_text:
Article 26

1. The Regional Government may provide financial assistance to community organizations, social organizations or non-governmental organizations that implement protection of women and children from discrimination and acts of violence.
2. Financial assistance as referred to in paragraph (1), is in accordance with regional financial capacity, and is implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations in the field of regional finance.

heading: CHAPTER XI
translated_text:
CHAPTER XI

CLOSING PROVISIONS

Article 27

This Regional Regulation comes into force on the date of promulgation.

So that everyone may know of it, the promulgation of this Regional Regulation is ordered by placing it in the Regional Gazette of the Special Capital Region Province of Jakarta.

Enacted in Jakarta on 14 November 2011

heading: ELUCIDATION

ELUCIDATION

OF

REGIONAL REGULATION OF THE SPECIAL CAPITAL REGION PROVINCE OF JAKARTA

NUMBER 8 OF 2011

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN FROM ACTS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

The position of DKI Jakarta Province as the national capital as stipulated in Law Number 29 of 2007 concerning the Government of the Special Capital Region Province of Jakarta as the Capital of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia, makes the city of Jakarta an attraction for some members of the community from various regions, thus giving rise to various social problems, including acts of violence against women and children both within the household and outside the household, such as torture or treatment that can degrade human dignity and worth.

Various acts of violence both against women and children both within the household and outside the household will destroy family life, society, government, nation, and state, therefore the Provincial Government of DKI Jakarta is obliged to provide protection to women and children from acts of violence which is an implementation of several laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

Protection of women and children from acts of violence is one of the obligations of the Regional Government as regulated in Article 22 letter a of Law Number 32 of 2004 concerning Regional Government. On that basis, the Provincial Government of DKI Jakarta has made various efforts to protect women and children from acts of violence, but has not been able to provide protection to women and children from various acts of violence, among others due to the still low understanding of the community regarding the rights of women and children, handling has not been well coordinated, its implementation has not been sustainable, and so on. Therefore, a Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children from Acts of Violence is needed to provide legal certainty in the protection of women and children from acts of violence.

The Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children from Acts of Violence, gives responsibility to the Regional Government starting from the prevention of acts of violence to the handling of victims of acts of violence. In its implementation the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments, and the community. In addition, adequate funding support both from the Government, Regional Government, as well as the participation of the business community and society, it is hoped that violence against women and children can be eliminated.

Letter a: The principle of humanity becomes the foundation of the concept of protection of women and children from acts of violence, which constitutes respect for human rights as well as the dignity and worth of every citizen and resident of Indonesia proportionally (the second principle of Pancasila).

Letter b: The principle of justice and gender equality, that gender justice is a process to be fair to men and women. Gender equality is the equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings, so that they are able to play a role and participate in political, economic, socio-cultural, governmental activities, and equality in enjoying the results of development.

Letter c: Protection is a principle that functions to provide protection to women and children in order to provide peace in family and community life.

Letter d: The principle of the best interests of women and children, that all actions concerning women and children carried out by families, communities, and Regional Governments are to fulfill the rights of women and children as regulated in laws and regulations.

Letter e: The principle of non-discrimination, that in providing protection to women and children from acts of violence there is no differentiation based on age, gender, race, ethnicity, tribe, religion and between groups.
